coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app has no tests at all, so none of the riskiest logic — filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting, data mapping, alternate-form exclusion — is covered by anything except the external acceptance suite.

evidence: app/src/lib/format.ts:10-44 — pure, behaviour-testable helpers exist but have zero assertions anywhere in app/
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests exist, so there is nothing to assess; the criterion cannot earn above the floor.

evidence: app/src/lib/browse.ts:59 — Math.min(Math.max(1, state.page), Math.max(1, pageCount)) clamp: any refactor bug here (e.g. off-by-one on last page, wrong empty-list handling) fails no app test
app/src/lib/api.ts:34-41 — semaphore queue and 60s TTL cache: a concurrency regression fails nothing
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.ts:17-23 — the missing-values-last branch bypasses the direction sign; a refactor could silently sort empty rows first with no failing test
regression_power.rationale: With zero tests in the app, no behaviour is protected; any refactor of the data layer or client scripts would be caught only if the external acceptance suite happens to cover that exact path.

evidence: app/src — no test files anywhere; nothing to generate noise or value
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also no signal; per the anchor, a test-less app scores 3 here.

findings.issue: Filtering (search substring, type, generation), 48-per-page pagination and the out-of-range page clamp have no tests; these are the app's most spec-sensitive, refactor-prone transformations.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests for browse() over a small fixture index: combined filters, empty results (pageCount 0), page beyond pageCount clamp, page 1 slice boundaries, and label-based case-insensitive matching (e.g. 'mr mime' matching 'Mr Mime').

findings.issue: cardsFor's alternate-form exclusion (id <= MAX_DEFAULT_POKEMON_ID), Map-based dedup and dex-number ordering are untested; a regression would put Mega forms in Learned-by/Pokémon lists or mis-order cards.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with refs including an id > 10000 form, duplicate refs and a species name that differs from the pokemon name (deoxys-normal → deoxys).

findings.issue: Client table sorting — direction flip, missing-values-last in both directions, stable tie-breaking and aria-sort bookkeeping — is untested DOM logic that someone will refactor.
findings.suggestion: Extract sortTable into a plain function over row data and unit test it with happy-dom/jsdom: missing values last ascending and descending, second click flips direction, non-sorted headers lose aria-sort.

findings.issue: URL state round-trip (stateFromParams/stateToSearch) is untested: page=0, page=abc, page=-1, omitted defaults all flow through here and drive both server routes and client popstate handling.
findings.suggestion: Property-style unit tests: stateToSearch(stateFromParams(qs)) normalizes every malformed and default input to the canonical form the spec requires.

findings.issue: The 404-vs-error distinction, TTL expiry, failed-promise cache eviction and the 24-slot semaphore are untested; a refactor of the cache could cache rejections or drop queued waiters.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getJson with a stubbed fetch: 404 resolves null, non-2xx throws ApiError, second call within TTL hits cache, rejected promise is not cached, and cache eviction under >5000 entries keeps fresh entries.

findings.issue: Species-index assembly — type slot ordering (slots.sort at line 183), generation assignment and species ordering — is untested; wrong slot ordering would silently reverse dual-type card labels.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getSpeciesIndex against a fixture API payload with a species whose types arrive out of slot order and a generation whose species list is unordered.

findings.issue: Version-group ordering and the default-game selection (highest order) plus moveRows' method ordering (level-up, machine, egg, tutor, then alphabetical) are untested spec-sensitive rules.
findings.suggestion: Unit test the game selection and method-ordering logic with a fixture including an out-of-order version group and an extra method like 'stadium-only'.

findings.issue: No error handling for API failures: mustGetJson throws ApiError (app/src/lib/api.ts:77) and there is no express error middleware, so an API 500 yields the framework's default error page — this path is untested and likely rough.
findings.suggestion: Add an error-mapping middleware plus a test that an upstream 500 renders a friendly error page rather than a stack-less express default.

findings.issue: Race-guard (latest ticket) and debounce logic for live filtering is untested; replacing the guard with naive awaits would interleave stale results under fast typing.
findings.suggestion: An integration test (Playwright or jsdom) typing quickly and asserting the final rendered list matches the last query would pin this behaviour.

findings.issue: Pure helpers (humanize, dexNumber, latestFlavorText taking the LAST English entry, idFromUrl, orDash) are the cheapest tests in the codebase and none exist; edge cases like empty strings, '—' for zero values and flavor text ordering are unguarded.
findings.suggestion: A ten-line unit file covering each helper's edge cases; orDash(0) in particular deserves a pinned assertion since 0 is falsy but a valid power.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no test script, no runner, no assertions — leaving all of its substantial, unit-testable logic (filtering, pagination, URL state, client sorting, data mapping, caching) guarded only by the external acceptance suite. Given how much of the code is pure functions, the omission is a clear choice rather than a constraint, and the first refactor of the data layer will be flying blind. I'd block merge on at least unit coverage for browse(), cardsFor() and the client sort.
